pool.sol: For a linear system to have infinitely many solutions, the equations must be proportional. Notice that \( \dfrac{3}{2} \) is the ratio of the \( x \)-coefficients. Equating the ratio of the \(y\)-coefficients gives \(\dfrac{-6}{-k} = \dfrac{3}{2} \implies \dfrac{6}{k} = \dfrac{3}{2} \implies 3k = 12\).

pool.sol: The line \( y = \frac{1}{2}x \) crosses the \( x \)-axis at \( (0,0) \). The line \( y = -2x + 10 \) crosses the \( x \)-axis at \( (5,0) \). pool.text: The line \( y = kx + 7 \) intersects the line \( y = -2x + 1 \) at a point with a positive \( x \)-coordinate and a positive \( y \)-coordinate. Which condition must \( k \) satisfy?

pool.text: What is the sum of the solutions to \( (x^2 - 3x)^2 - 2(x^2 - 3x) - 8 = 0 \)?

pool.sol: Let \( u = x^2 - 3x \): \( u^2 - 2u - 8 = 0 \implies (u - 4)(u + 2) = 0 \implies u = 4 \text{ or } u = -2 \). Case 1: \( x^2 - 3x = 4 \implies x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0 \) has discriminant \( 9 + 16 = 25 > 0 \) (2 real roots with sum 3). Case 2: \( x^2 - 3x = -2 \implies x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0 \) has discriminant \( 9 - 8 = 1 > 0 \) (2 real roots with sum 3). The sum of all 4 real solutions is \( 3 + 3 = 6 \).
hints: Let \( u = x^2 - 3x \): \( u^2 - 2u - 8 = 0 \implies (u - 4)(u + 2) = 0 \implies u = 4 \text{ or } u = -2 \).

Case 1: \( x^2 - 3x = 4 \implies x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0 \) has discriminant \( 9 + 16 = 25 > 0 \) (2 real roots with sum 3). Case 2: \( x^2 - 3x = -2 \implies x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0 \) has discriminant \( 9 - 8 = 1 > 0 \) (2 real roots with sum 3).
The sum of all 4 real solutions is \(3 + 3\).

pool.sol: Let \( u = x^2 \). Then the equation becomes \( u^2 - 13u + 36 = 0 \). Factor: \( (u - 9)(u - 4) = 0 \implies u = 9 \) or \( u = 4 \). Since \( u = x^2 \), we have \( x^2 = 9 \implies x = \pm 3 \), and \( x^2 = 4 \implies x = \pm 2 \). The largest positive value of \( x \) is 3.

The largest positive value of \(x\) is 3.

pool.text: A circle is centered at \( (2, 3) \) and is tangent to the horizontal line \( y = 7 \). What is the area of the circle?
pool.educational_aim: Synthesize One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error with related mathematical concepts to solve high-difficulty past-paper synthesis, optimization, proof, or modeling problems.

pool.sol: The radius is the perpendicular distance from the center \( (2, 3) \) to the horizontal line \( y = 7 \), which is \( |7 - 3| = 4 \). The area of the circle is \( \pi r^2 = \pi (4^2) = 16\pi \).
hints: The radius is the perpendicular distance from the center \( (2, 3) \) to the horizontal line \( y = 7 \).
The area of the circle is \(\pi r^2 = \pi (4^2)\).

pool.text: In a circle with radius 12, an arc has a central angle of \( 60^\circ \). What is the length of the arc divided by \( \pi \)?

pool.sol: Arc length formula: \( s = \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi r = \dfrac{60}{360} \times 2\pi(12) = \dfrac{1}{6} \times 24\pi = 4\pi \). Dividing by \( \pi \) yields 4.
hints: Arc length formula: \(s = \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi r\).
Substitute and simplify: \(s = \dfrac{60}{360} \times 2\pi(12)\). Compute the final value from: \(\dfrac{1}{6} \times 24\pi\).
Dividing by \(\pi\) yields 4.

pool.text: Two similar triangles have corresponding side lengths in the ratio 3:5. If the area of the smaller triangle is 36, what is the area of the larger triangle?
pool.educational_aim: Demonstrate foundational mastery of Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations by solving direct algebraic, graphical, or geometric formulations tested on SAT past papers.
pool.exam_archetype: Equivalent Expressions & Quadratic Equations — Direct Concept & Representation
pool.sol: The ratio of areas of similar figures is the square of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions: \( \text{Area Ratio} = \left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{9}{25} \). Set up the proportion: \( \dfrac{36}{\text{Area}_{\text{large}}} = \dfrac{9}{25} \implies \text{Area}_{\text{large}} = \dfrac{36 \times 25}{9} = 4 \times 25 = 100 \).
hints: The ratio of areas of similar figures is the square of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions: \(\text{Area Ratio} = \left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^2\).
Set up the proportion: \(\dfrac{36}{\text{Area}_{\text{large}}} = \dfrac{9}{25}\). Substitute and simplify: \(\text{Area}_{\text{large}} = \dfrac{36 \times 25}{9}\).
Evaluate the simplified expression: \(\text{Area}_{\text{large}} = 4 \times 25\).

Compute the final value from: \(70 \times \dfrac{1}{2}\).
